title: Start the next clip from the previous clip's end picture
rule: Begin every continuing clip from the exact end picture of the clip before it, never from a fresh text-only prompt.
why: Frame hand-off is the one continuity signal every vendor and practitioner describes; it fixes the place, light and subject at the join.
how: Pass the approved end picture as the start image; the prompt describes only what happens next.

title: Draw an end picture from the picture before it
rule: Make each end picture by editing or referencing the picture that starts the clip, not by drawing it from text alone.
why: Edit-style image models keep objects and characters stable across repeated edits, so the end state is the same world one step on.
how: Give the start picture as the anchor and the state sentence of the end as the change; say 'keep everything else the same'.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js makeFrame (end picture anchored on the previous picture)

title: Keep both frames compatible in light, perspective and scale
rule: Check that a start and an end picture share aspect ratio, horizon, subject scale and lighting before sending them to a first/last frame model.
why: Mismatched anchors make the model warp geometry or flicker to bridge the gap.
how: Reject or redraw an end picture that changes lens, light direction or time of day without a reason in the story.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js CONTINUITY_SYSTEM checks light and time-of-day jumps in text; pictures themselves are not compared
monofilm.idea: Compare start and end pictures for horizon, scale and colour before a clip is released.

title: Change one thing between the start and end picture
rule: Let an end picture differ from its start in one stage of change only (a pose, one prop state), not several events.
why: A short clip can only show a small change; the target frame is a guide, not a jump cut, and 5 second clips transition more cleanly than long ones.
how: One sentence per state, each a frozen picture; split a two-event change across two clips.

title: Describe the destination in the prompt as well as in the end picture
rule: State both the opening beat and the end state in words when using first/last frame control.
why: The model respects both anchors better when the text names both.
how: One sentence of action that goes from the start state to the end state, no new objects.

monofilm.where: src/wizard.js makeFrame uses states; composeClip beat covers the action
monofilm.idea: Always put the end state's words into the clip prompt as the landing, not only the picture.

title: Stop at 3 to 6 seconds of change per generation
rule: Keep each generated clip short (about 3 to 8 seconds) and chain, rather than ask for one long take.
why: Instruction following and consistency fall off with length; users and vendors both advise stitching short clips.
how: Plan a scene as several clips of one beat each; 'one action per shot'.

title: Do not extend from a frame-only hand-off for long chains
rule: For more than two or three chained clips, add references (character, location) in addition to the last frame.
why: A last frame alone lacks identity, place and camera context; extension from one frame loses them step by step.
how: Pass the character picture and the location picture with every clip, as well as the start picture.

monofilm.where: src/mcp-video.js clipSpec returns references plus start_picture; models without references use the prompt sentences
monofilm.idea: Use stage references per clip for models that accept them.

title: Restate the full identity and place in every clip prompt
rule: Repeat the same short wording for each character, the place and the light in every clip; never shorten it for later clips.
why: Shortened descriptions in later segments drift (long hair became short); consistent wording keeps the model on the same ground.
how: Reuse fixed one-line descriptions from the film's cast and place records, word for word.

title: Check consistency after every clip, not at the end
rule: Review each new clip against the previous one before generating the next.
why: Drift in colour, background and light accumulates; errors from an unreviewed clip become the next clip's input.
how: Compare last frame of clip N with the first frame of clip N+1 and the scene's state sentence; redo before moving on.

monofilm.idea: Auto-compare the take's last frame to the planned end picture and flag colour or object changes.

title: Fix drift cause: bad conditioning, not just bad luck
rule: When a chain degrades, rebuild the hand-off from a clean approved picture rather than from the last generated frame.
why: Research finds drift comes from self-generated conditioning carrying errors; cleaner conditioning stops the build-up.
how: Use the planned end picture (an approved still) as the next start, not a frame grabbed from the video.

title: Keep the approved still as the hand-off, not the video frame
rule: Prefer chaining through an approved still image over extending the video file.
why: A still is sharp and artifact free; extension regenerates the join frames, which are often smeared or off-model.
how: Generate end pictures first (storyboard of keyframes), then clips between them.

title: Plan keyframes for the whole film before generating motion
rule: Draw the keyframes of all clips first, review them as a storyboard, then make the motion.
why: Showing all keyframes at once lets a person fix one frame without touching approved ones, and the planned story stays consistent.
how: Review a keyframe sheet; regenerate single frames; only then spend video credits.

title: Choose the chaining frame before the clip slows down
rule: When taking a frame from a take to start the next clip, pick it before the motion decelerates, and generate extra seconds for it.
why: Models ease to a stop at the end, so a literal last frame restarts from rest and hitches; matched pixels are not matched speed.
how: Generate 1 to 2 seconds more than needed; trim the settled tail in the edit.

monofilm.idea: Tell the generator to keep moving through the last frame when the next clip continues the action.

title: Trim the first frames of a continued clip
rule: Cut the first one to two frames of a clip that continues another.
why: Join frames are often duplicated, smeared or off-model; usable motion starts about frame three.
how: Trim 2 frames at each join in assembly and check at full speed.

monofilm.where: assembly.trim_start_frames in get_clip and clip.json
monofilm.idea: Apply the trim in an assembly step

title: Hide the cut with motion and cut on action
rule: Put a join where something moves, not on a still frame, and cut mid-action.
why: A still shows small colour and background mismatches; motion hides them.
how: Plan hold shots with no static join; for a cut, cut during a body or camera move.

monofilm.idea: Choose edit points inside motion when assembling.

title: Lock light, time of day and weather in a fixed prompt slot
rule: Put the light, time of day and weather in the same slot of every clip prompt and in every state sentence, and change them only on purpose.
why: Each generation is graded alone; fixed words and a reference carry the look across clips.
how: Name numeric colour temperature or 3 to 5 palette colours; open with the same style block.

title: Make the establishing wide first and use it as the place reference
rule: Generate a clean wide picture of each location once and use it as the reference for every shot there.
why: A simple uncluttered scene reference holds location better than words; busy scenes warp.
how: One approved place picture per location; change one variable per shot.

title: Give the first picture of a scene the last picture of the scene before
rule: Use the previous scene's final picture as a reference for the next scene's first picture, so light and colour carry over the cut.
why: Scenes drawn independently differ in grade and light.
how: Pass it as an anchor with a note to match light, colours and time of day.

title: Track the state of every counted or changing object
rule: List each tracked object with one fixed look and its state at every clip boundary, and check that the action that causes each change is shown.
why: History forgetting means models lose earlier content; stating state per boundary keeps counts and stages right.
how: state[k] per boundary; check the cause comes before the effect (cap off before bubble).

title: Name only the objects that are in view at a boundary
rule: In a state sentence or a clip prompt, name only things visible at that moment.
why: Naming something that is not there yet makes a generator draw it; extension also needs a character named again if they left the recent context.
how: Filter props per clip; re-name a character if absent from the last 10 seconds.

title: Use a cut for scene changes and a hand-off only for the same shot
rule: Chain clips only inside one continuous shot; use a new start picture after a cut.
why: Extension continues the last frame, so abrupt place or camera changes look wrong.

title: Do not rely on an end frame in a multi-shot generation
rule: If a model's multi-shot mode ignores end images, generate each shot as its own first/last frame clip.
why: Kling's end image works only in single-prompt mode, not with multi-prompt, so end-frame control and multi-shot do not combine.
how: Check each model's controls before choosing the plan; keep a per-model profile.

title: Match frame size and counts to the model's grid
rule: Prepare keyframes at the model's size and frame-count rules (e.g. 8n+1 frames, sizes divisible by 32 in LTX) before generating.
why: Off-grid keyframes give odd results or errors.
how: Resize every picture to the target size first.

monofilm.idea: Put per-model size and frame rules in the generator profile.

title: Normalise size, frame rate and colour before joining clips
rule: Bring every clip to one resolution, frame rate and aspect ratio, and one grade, before the assembly.
why: Joining does not fix continuity; mismatched settings show as stutter, and each generation can drift in colour even within one clip.
how: Check each take's measures; apply one grade pass to the sequence.

monofilm.where: src/mcp-video.js clipSpec returns aspect and fps per clip
monofilm.idea: Normalise take size, fps and colour in the final assembly step.

title: Use a crossfade or an overlap only when two clips clash
rule: Join continuing clips with a hard cut when the hand-off is clean, and add a short overlap crossfade only when a small mismatch remains.
why: Overlap and a short blend hide small differences; hard cuts on motion are cleaner.
how: Generate a little past the cut; fade for a few frames.

monofilm.idea: Offer a 2 to 6 frame crossfade option at a join.

title: Anchor a long chain on the first approved picture
rule: For a long chain, keep returning to one approved first picture of the scene as the anchor, not only the latest frame.
why: Research uses the first frame as the stable anchor and keeps long-range memory to stop drift.
how: Pass the scene start picture and character picture as references to later clips.

monofilm.where: clipSpec references and scene start picture; chain uses previous end picture
monofilm.idea: Pass the scene's first picture as an extra reference in later clips of a long scene.

title: Review a join at full speed and frame by frame
rule: Judge every join twice: at playing speed and frame by frame.
why: A clean paused frame can jitter in playback, and a matching frame can hide a velocity break.
how: Log the first and last bad frame; redo only that clip.

monofilm.where: takes have measures (smooth, cuts, hold) recorded by npm run measure
monofilm.idea: Compare motion across the join, not only the pictures.
